target.title: refactor: centralize bounded file reads in fs-safe
target.body:
Related: #110594
Related: #110591
Related: #110592
Related: #110516
Related: openclaw/fs-safe#41
Related: openclaw/fs-safe#43

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw owned duplicate asynchronous and synchronous loops for allocation-bounded reads from file descriptors that had already been opened and pinned by a filesystem boundary. That duplicated policy now owned by fs-safe and made the byte-limit/error contract easier for the two implementations to drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

This routes all eight descriptor-read consumers through the existing boundary-file facade and delegates incremental reads to the published fs-safe advanced API. The facade preserves OpenClaw's established `RangeError` message for oversized files, while the duplicate 63-line reader is deleted. The eighth caller is the exec-approvals file reader that landed on `main` while this PR was under review; rebasing this branch brought it under the same shared boundary.

The dependency is pinned to `@openclaw/fs-safe@0.4.3`. OpenClaw's downstream `EPERM` fsync patch and patch allowlist entry are removed because that compatibility fix now ships upstream. Both lockfiles and the Plugin SDK API baseline are regenerated from the published artifact, and the package-patch test fixture no longer treats the removed fs-safe patch as approved.

Downstream exact-head CI against 0.4.2 exposed an error-message compatibility regression in the existing regular-file readers. fs-safe PR #43 restored that contract without losing the bounded allocation behavior, and 0.4.3 is the corrected patch release consumed here.

## User Impact

There is no intended user-visible behavior change. Config input, secrets plans, exec-approvals files, agent message files, local avatars, hook metadata, and workspace bootstrap files retain their existing size limits and overflow messages while sharing fs-safe's allocation-bounded implementation.

## Evidence

- Published dependency: [@openclaw/fs-safe@0.4.3](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openclaw/fs-safe/v/0.4.3), [GitHub Release](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/releases/tag/v0.4.3), integrity `sha512-COOPvc0yFwisi0QXA4FtKz5LLzT+1reYNNJn+598/PHYPCxo4uS8NZS4BQV62ypqxL7laW702PitCKyEXu5MpA==`.
- fs-safe PR #43 passed the Node 22/24 Linux/macOS/Windows matrix, coverage, and benchmarks. Exact 0.4.3 release-commit CI: [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/actions/runs/29673148751) and [coverage](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/actions/runs/29673148750).
- Exact OpenClaw head `184be3349ae708e02ff95b925e94bf8836a779a1`: a fresh Blacksmith Testbox accepted the frozen lockfile, installed the published 0.4.3 package, and passed 80 tests across all seven downstream regression and integration files.
- Exact OpenClaw head: full `pnpm build` passed, including CLI bootstrap imports, Plugin SDK exports, runtime postbuild, and Control UI budgets.
- Exact OpenClaw head: full `pnpm check:changed` passed in 8m31s, including all shrinkwrap guards, the full TypeScript project graph, every Oxlint shard, Plugin SDK contracts, patch/database guards, and runtime import cycles.
- Fresh whole-branch Codex autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings (correctness confidence 0.88).
- `git diff --check` passed.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the implementation, dependency source/API, generated artifacts, and test evidence.
